heading.en: Why do flower prices jump at festivals?

hook.en: Before Dasara, the price of marigold flowers shoots up; after a bumper harvest, tomato prices crash. *Shifts in demand* and supply explain both.
hook.kn: ದಸರಾ ಮೊದಲು ಚೆಂಡು ಹೂವಿನ ಬೆಲೆ ಗಗನಕ್ಕೇರುತ್ತದೆ; ಭಾರಿ ಫಸಲಿನ ನಂತರ ಟೊಮೆಟೊ ಬೆಲೆ ಕುಸಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪೂರೈಕೆಯ ಸರಿತಗಳು ಎರಡನ್ನೂ ವಿವರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: Before Dasara, the price of marigold flowers shoots up; after a bumper harvest, tomato prices crash. Shifts in demand and supply explain both. In this lesson: Show the effect of a shift in demand on equilibrium.
Show the effect of a shift in supply on equilibrium.
Calculate the new equilibrium.

body.en: With the number of firms fixed, if demand increases (rightward shift, for example because income rises for a normal good or tastes change), there is excess demand at the old price, so both equilibrium price and quantity rise. If demand decreases (leftward shift), there is excess supply at the old price, so both equilibrium price and quantity fall.

narration.en: If demand increases, equilibrium price and quantity both rise. If demand decreases, both fall.

body.en: If supply increases (rightward shift, for example because of better technology, lower input prices or a good harvest), there is excess supply at the old price, so equilibrium price falls and quantity rises. If supply decreases (leftward shift, for example because of a unit tax or crop failure), equilibrium price rises and quantity falls.

narration.en: If supply increases, price falls and quantity rises. If supply decreases, price rises and quantity falls.

problem.en: qD = 300 − 10p, qS = 50 + 15p. (a) Income rises and demand becomes qD = 350 − 10p. (b) Instead, technology improves and supply becomes qS = 100 + 15p. Find the new equilibrium in each case.

answer.en: (a) p = ₹12, q = 230 (both rise); (b) p = ₹8, q = 220 (price falls, quantity rises).

explanation.en: 400 − 10p = 50 + 15p gives 25p = 350, p = ₹14 (it was ₹10 before the rise).
